sections.content: How many people stayed in Cheadle Hulme after gaining qualifications?

Cheadle Hulme is a medium-sized town in the North West. Cheadle Hulme does not have its own university.

Cheadle Hulme has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Cheadle Hulme ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,060 state-school pupils from Cheadle Hulme who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 530 (50%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 345 (33%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Cheadle Hulme to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Cheadle Hulme's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Cheadle Hulme in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Cheadle Hulme move to?

Of Cheadle Hulme's graduates, 200 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 110 of those graduates (55%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Cheadle Hulme's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 130 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 105 of those qualified non-graduates (81%) were living fairly locally, in the Manchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Cheadle Hulme's GCSE cohort:

  • 95 graduates left the North West
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 17% of graduates and 20% of qualified non-graduates living in Cheadle Hulme had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 380 graduates and 255 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Cheadle Hulme. This is compared with the 530 graduates and 345 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 83% of the graduates had also lived in Cheadle Hulme as GCSE pupils, while 17% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Cheadle Hulme in 2018 to 2019, 80% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 20% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
